We are systematically investigating the different routes within this program. Please review the project description in /04_boundary_winding/threshold_routes/README.md.

Please record your research within the relevant notes folders. Progress will be updated in /04_boundary_winding/threshold_routes/09_expanding_contour_later_collision/research-progress/01_EXPANDING_CONTOUR_PROGRESS_20261020.md, and chat histories within the relevant subfolder.
Please continue the investigation. When you finish a task, record the progress in 01_EXPANDING_CONTOUR_PROGRESS_20261020.md, and continue until all tasks are finished or you run out of compute budget.
I’ll read the research program, route overview, and repository workflow, then continue the open tasks and record the results in the relevant notes and progress log.

The program’s first round is still unstarted. I’ll first fix the finite-contour contract and test its winding calculation against the prescribed controls. In parallel, I’ll assess whether the proposed theta-source remainder can supply a new signed estimate before doing any large computation.

A key limitation is emerging: if the regularized field stays within distance one of \(1\) on the boundary, its winding is zero. A successful estimate must therefore retain signed phase information beyond a small remainder bound. The control replay is also checking that the contour accounts for wall crossings and the initial multiplicity correctly.

The exact control replay gives the required outcomes: the quadratic has no later collision, the fourth-order event contributes its full initial index, and the two-event example registers an additional collision. A cubic control also matches arbitrary nonzero \(h_2\) and arbitrary \(h_3\) while having no later event, sharpening the test of what extra source information is needed.

The root-following alternative gives an exact reduction: its walls contribute no phase, and the cap winding is determined by how many extra real roots lie between them. This identifies the missing input—a new arithmetic estimate of that root count. I’m recording the result alongside the source-remainder obstruction and checking both before updating the task statuses.

The main notes and control record are saved. I’m checking one additional bounded case: whether the existing theta evaluator can rigorously exclude an event in the previously proposed box \(T=0.1\pm10^{-6}\), \(a\in[1001,1002]\). I’ll verify coverage and error bounds first; an exclusion there would be recorded separately from a winding gain.

The small event box lies outside the inherited certified cover. Extending the evaluator requires a substantially larger spatial error allowance—about \(2.1\times10^{-7}\) in its fixed normalization. The four-cell check is using that allowance and rechecking the omitted-source bounds; the earlier error bound cannot be reused.

The bounded theta check passed. The complete first jet is nonzero throughout \(T\in[0.099999,0.100001]\), \(a\in[1001,1002]\), excluding collisions of every multiplicity in that box. Its normalized lower margin exceeds \(4.1345\times10^{-4}\), after a complete error allowance below \(2.0839\times10^{-7}\). This is a small finite exclusion; the signed contour estimate remains open.

The notes, certificates, and separate same-model review are complete. I’m updating the progress log and indexes to keep the results distinct: a new finite event exclusion, a verified contour consumer, and scoped limits of the tested estimating methods. The later-collision estimate remains open, so the infinity-cap and multiplicity extensions stay deferred.

Completed the bounded first round and updated the [progress log](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/threshold_routes/09_expanding_contour_later_collision/research-progress/01_EXPANDING_CONTOUR_PROGRESS_20261020.md).

- **New finite exclusion:** certified \(H>0\) throughout \(t\in[0.099999,0.100001]\), \(x\in[1001,1002]\), excluding collisions of every multiplicity there.
- Verified the complete contour calculation with 18 exact controls and three required refusals.
- Established precise limitations of unsigned remainder estimates and root-following walls.

Saved four research notes, reproducible certificates, a separate same-model review, and progress updates; refreshed the chat history.

The signed theta estimate forcing a later collision remains open. The infinite-cap and multiplicity extensions remain deferred pending that input.
What is the bottleneck on the signed theta estimate forcing a later collision? Does the idea work or is it stalled on some structural issue?
I’ll check the recorded obstruction and source estimates to distinguish a limitation of the tested method from a structural problem with the contour idea.

**The contour construction works as a rigorous detector of later collisions. We have not found a theta-specific mechanism that forces one. The current unsigned estimating method has a proved structural obstruction; the broader signed approach remains open.**

For an initial ordinary double event, the complete physical winding is
\[
W_J=-1-K_{\mathrm{later}}.
\]
Removing the initial contribution gives \(W_Z=-K_{\mathrm{later}}\). We therefore need an independently established **negative upper bound for \(W_Z\)**. The contour geometry and index accounting now support that implication.

The bottleneck is obtaining the extra negative turn from theta arithmetic. Two findings explain why the approaches tested so far cannot supply it:

- **Smaller unsigned remainders cannot force the desired winding.** If the nonzero boundary field satisfies \(|Z-1|\le1\), its winding is exactly zero. Larger disks centered at \(1\) still admit the constant field \(Z=1\), so those disk bounds alone cannot force negative winding either. A successful estimate must control a substantial excursion from the initial model **and its direction**. More precision within the same unsigned information class cannot fix this. The cubic controls also show that heat flow and the prescribed initial \(h_2,h_3\) alone permit a genuine threshold with no later collision. [Source-estimate audit](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/threshold_routes/09_expanding_contour_later_collision/notes/01_FINITE_CONTOUR_AND_SOURCE_CONTRACT_20261020.md)

- **Following roots moves the missing estimate to the cap.** The walls contribute zero phase, but the resulting winding is \(-N/2\), where \(N\) counts additional roots between the terminal endpoints. We still need theta arithmetic to force \(N\ge2\). Choosing root-following walls does not establish that count. [Root-wall analysis](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/threshold_routes/09_expanding_contour_later_collision/notes/03_ROOT_FOLLOWING_WALLS_AND_CAP_COUNT_20261020.md)

What could advance the idea is a **signed approximation retaining the complete theta coefficients**, whose boundary winding is already negative and whose total error is smaller than its boundary separation—or an equivalent certified oriented-crossing count. We have neither yet, and no negative phase margin currently exists to refine.

My assessment is that the idea is **a sound framework with an unresolved central arithmetic step**. Further contour refinements alone are unlikely to advance it. The small box exclusion adds finite coverage, but supplies no evidence that the missing signed estimate will succeed.
Are there other topological invariants that might be relevant, or is the signed winding the most relevant one for this argument? Is there an energy type term that could be more useful?
I’ll compare the other invariants and energy quantities already studied in the repository, then assess whether any gives a stronger way to force the later collision.

For this boundary field, winding already captures all the homotopy information. The more useful alternative may be a signed energy estimate: the Laguerre expression directly controls phase, while ordinary positive energies lose the sign we need. Zero-interaction energies are also relevant, but their natural forward evolution resists collisions, so they still need a new theta-specific argument.

I found a concrete energy estimate worth testing: a localized average of \(Q=H_x^2-HH_{xx}\). Integration by parts lets us express it using only \(H\) and \(H_x\), which could reduce the derivative data needed. Localization matters—the unweighted average is automatically nonnegative. I’m recording this as an estimate to investigate; no negative theta bound has been obtained.

The independent mathematical check found no blocking error in these identities. It also confirms a useful distinction: a negative localized Laguerre average would contradict future all-realness directly, without needing to force a second real collision first. That makes it a plausible alternative to compare with the contour method, though the required theta-specific negative estimate remains open.

**Signed winding is the right topological invariant for the present argument. A signed energy estimate could offer a more useful analytic route—but we do not yet have the theta estimate that would make it work.**

For the boundary field \(J=H+iH_x\), a nonvanishing loop takes values in \(\mathbb C^\times\), whose homotopy classes are completely classified by winding. Other descriptions largely recover the same information:

- The projective direction \([H:H_x]\) has degree twice the winding.
- Root counts with moving-wall flux give the same index accounting.
- Spectral flow or a Maslov index would require additional structure; their usefulness would depend on estimates that structure provides.
- A complex argument-principle contour could detect later **nonreal zeros**, but would require different complex boundary data.

The most relevant energy-like quantity is the **signed Laguerre expression**
\[
Q=H_x^2-HH_{xx}.
\]
It directly controls the spatial phase:
\[
\partial_x\arg(H+iH_x)=-\frac{Q}{H^2+H_x^2}.
\]
For the theta family, future all-realness implies \(Q\ge0\). Thus a conditional estimate forcing \(Q<0\) at a later point would contradict the threshold assumption directly. It could **bypass the need to force a second real collision**. This is the existing BW-05 alternative.

A concrete energy version deserves consideration. For a fixed nonnegative smooth compactly supported weight \(\psi\), integration by parts gives
\[
\boxed{
A_\psi(t)=\int\psi Q\,dx
=2\int\psi H_x^2\,dx-\frac12\int\psi''H^2\,dx.
}
\]
A negative \(A_\psi\) forces a negative \(Q\) somewhere. Its potential advantage is that evaluation requires only \(H\) and \(H_x\), and one signed scalar bound might be easier than controlling an entire contour. The costs are cancellation, spatial integration, and errors amplified by derivatives of the weight. No practical advantage has yet been demonstrated.

**Localization is essential.** Under suitable decay,
\[
\int Q\,dx=2\int H_x^2\,dx\ge0.
\]
So the ordinary unweighted energy loses precisely the sign we need. Likewise, a large positive angular energy cannot force winding: a phase can oscillate arbitrarily much and return with zero net rotation.

Zero-interaction energies are another serious possibility. In a finite all-real root system, logarithmic repulsion produces a decreasing interaction energy that resists forward collisions. For theta’s infinite root system, one needs renormalization and control of exterior contributions. Rodgers–Tao successfully used such energy methods to prove \(\Lambda\ge0\); that proof does not reverse to give the desired \(\Lambda\le0\). [Primary paper](https://arxiv.org/html/1801.05914).

My recommendation is to retain winding as the collision detector and compare **one explicit localized signed Laguerre functional** against the pointwise BW-05 approach. The missing ingredient remains an estimate using the unchanged theta source and hypothetical event constraints that produces a strict negative margin. Changing the invariant or introducing a positive energy alone does not supply it.

I recorded the identities, control checks, and limitations in [Note 05](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/threshold_routes/09_expanding_contour_later_collision/notes/05_TOPOLOGICAL_ALTERNATIVES_AND_ENERGY_OBSERVATIONS_20261020.md), obtained a separate same-model mathematical review, and updated the progress register.

The BW-05 approach also sounds promising. The zero interaction energy seems like a useful tool to keep in mind as well. 

Let's consider any simplifications that can occur along a heat flow contour. On a notational point, I'm thinking maybe we should call it a heat flow contour instead of a light cone contour. Naturally my intuition comes from physics, where you have causality in a medium (speed of light). Here I think since we are dealing with the heat equation it is probably more akin to heat flow, so maybe heat flow contour is more appropriate. Let me know if you agree with this terminology.

I think the idea of a heat flow contour should be taken literally. From the heat equation, how does heat propagate. Is there some natural intuition for what could require a previous collision? Perhaps there is a different contour we should be looking at. If you look at the collision path of the two particles that collide at time T=\Lambda, you could split the contour into a triangle that contains the collision (or a triangle with curved sides), and the rest. The rest must be topologically trivial and the triangle must contain the full -1 winding. Perhaps there is some contradiction that can be found from that splitting, or some clever variant.

I agree with “heat flow contour”; it avoids suggesting a finite propagation speed. I’ll examine your proposed split along the colliding zero paths, including which parts of the winding it fixes and whether a different contour could expose a useful signed estimate.

Your split is valid once the collision is enclosed rather than left on the contour’s tip. The key subtlety is that the remainder can have zero total index while still carrying phase circulation around the removed collision. I also found a useful simplification: along simple zero paths, the jet’s phase is constant, so those sides contribute exactly zero.

The heat direction matters here: \(H_t=-H_{xx}\), so ordinary diffusion runs toward decreasing \(t\). The real pair splits as \(t\) increases and collides when followed backward. Taking diffusion literally also gives a useful alternative: Gaussian averages on a later slice recover the earlier jet, and the two collision conditions imply a sharp energy inequality on that slice. I’m checking that inequality against the quadratic and cubic controls.

Two concrete simplifications survived the checks. A curved side defined by a nonzero level of \(H\) makes its phase contribution depend only on its endpoints. Separately, a double collision requires \(\int G_s H^2\le s\int G_s H_x^2\) on every later Gaussian-weighted slice. The quadratic saturates this bound, so heat flow alone gives no contradiction; a certified violation for theta would exclude the proposed initial collision.

The checks support using the split to simplify the calculation, but the single-collision quadratic realizes the entire split consistently. The Gaussian inequality gives a different test: it asks whether a later profile could have come from the proposed earlier double zero. I’m saving both derivations and a diagram, with the distinction between these identities and the still-missing theta estimate made explicit.

**I agree with “heat flow contour,” or “parabolic heat flow contour” when we mean the square-root opening. Your proposed splitting is valid once the collision is enclosed, and it gives useful simplifications. The splitting alone is consistent with exactly one collision, however.**

The time direction needs care. Our equation is
\[
H_t=-H_{xx},
\]
so ordinary diffusion runs toward **decreasing \(t\)**. Near an ordinary collision,
\[
x_\pm(t)=a\pm\sqrt{2(t-T)}+O(t-T).
\]
The real pair therefore splits as \(t\) increases, and collides when followed backward toward \(T\). Immediately below \(T\), the corresponding zeros are complex.

The square-root scale is genuinely diffusive. But the heat kernel has nonzero tails everywhere: there is no finite boundary beyond which influences vanish. That is why “heat flow contour” fits better than “light cone.” [Nolen’s diffusion notes](https://math.stanford.edu/~ryzhik/STANFORD/STANF227-11/notes227-09.pdf).

Your curved triangle has a particularly clean realization. Follow the two simple zero paths, close them with a later cap, and **round the bottom below the collision**. The rounding is essential: putting the collision directly on the tip makes physical winding undefined.

For the exact model \(H=y^2-2\tau\), the contributions are:

- Each zero-path side: **zero phase change**, since \(J=iH_x\) stays on one imaginary ray.
- The cap between the adjacent roots: **\(-\pi\)**.
- The rounded lower connector: **\(-\pi\)**.

Thus the enclosed region carries exactly the full winding \(-1\).

![Rounded heat flow contour and its winding](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/threshold_routes/09_expanding_contour_later_collision/notes/figures/HEAT_FLOW_LENS_20261020.png)

This model has only one collision, and its complementary region contains none. So it realizes your proposed decomposition without contradiction.

There is also a distinction in “the rest is topologically trivial.” If the remainder contains no other common zero of \(H,H_x\), its **total boundary index** is zero. An annular remainder can nevertheless retain circulation around the removed collision: its inner and outer boundary contributions cancel. Zero total index does not mean every remaining arc has zero phase contribution.

Physically, the zero paths are not insulating walls either. Although \(H=0\) there, \(H_x\) is generally nonzero, so heat crosses them. Ordinary diffusion can erase the signed lobe between them without requiring an earlier collision that created it.

Two variants seem worth retaining.

**First, follow a nonzero level of \(H\) for the curved side.** Normalize \(F=H/h_2\), and choose the side \(F=\varepsilon>0\). Then
\[
J/h_2=\varepsilon+iF_x.
\]
Its phase remains in the right half-plane, so the entire curved-side contribution is determined by its endpoints. If the closing cap contains \(N\) simple zeros, the complete winding is exactly \(-N/2\). This simplifies the boundary calculation; forcing another collision still requires an independent estimate giving \(N\ge4\), rather than the original two.

**Second, literal heat propagation gives a useful Gaussian energy test.** Let
\[
f(y)=H(T+s,a+y),\qquad
G_s(y)=\frac{e^{-y^2/(4s)}}{\sqrt{4\pi s}}.
\]
A double zero at \((T,a)\) forces the constant and linear Gaussian moments of \(f\) to vanish. Consequently,
\[
\boxed{\int G_s f^2\,dy\ \le\ s\int G_s(f')^2\,dy.}
\]
This is a sharp inequality: the quadratic collision model attains equality.

It provides a concrete way to ask whether a later profile could have come from the proposed earlier collision. If a complete theta estimate at a **fixed** \(s>0\) proved
\[
s\int G_sH_x^2-\int G_sH^2<0,
\]
the initial collision would be excluded directly. These are whole-line integrals; any finite implementation must pay the Gaussian tails. No such negative theta margin has yet been obtained.

I recorded the derivations, controls, and diagram in [Note 06](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-3/13_contradiction_analysis/04_boundary_winding/threshold_routes/09_expanding_contour_later_collision/notes/06_HEAT_FLOW_CONTOURS_AND_GAUSSIAN_CAP_ENERGY_20261020.md), obtained a separate same-model mathematical review, updated progress, and adopted “heat flow contour” prospectively.

I’ll write a research program and progress register for the heat flow contours and Gaussian cap estimates, then prepare a self-contained manuscript covering the results and their limits. I’ll keep only the TeX source for the manuscript.

The manuscript will distinguish proved identities, the bounded numerical exclusion, and the estimates that remain open. I’m including proofs for the contour and energy results so the exposition can be read independently of the notes, while preserving the limits of the numerical evidence.

The program now has explicit stopping rules and comparison tests: a Gaussian estimate must produce a certified margin or a measurable advantage over the direct first-jet estimate. I’m also making the manuscript’s numerical section explicit about its source data and error bounds, so the small certified exclusion is not mistaken for progress on the global collision claim.

The manuscript draft now covers the index theorem, contour controls, heat-flow splitting, Laguerre identities, and Gaussian energy test. I’m adding the exact numerical input table and checking the draft for mathematical and compilation errors. The manuscript will remain a single TeX file.

The manuscript compiles successfully. The mathematical review found no blocking error; it prompted a few clarifications about boundary nonvanishing, integrability, and quadrature settings. I’m applying those corrections and linking the new documents into the progress register and draft history. No new theta estimate is being claimed.

The three documents are saved, and the corrected manuscript compiles successfully. Its folder contains only `main.tex`. The progress registers now distinguish this completed documentation work from the still-unstarted numerical energy tests; I’m finishing the chat-history record.
